messages:
miles: Heads-up — acme-prod hit per-key limits yesterday and got throttled. They want a temporary bump for a marketing burst. Thinking we add a "shadow" override mode: allow elevated throughput for a short TTL but keep billing/alerts and an easy revoke. Anyone strongly against?

devon: Can you spell out the semantics? shadow = bypass enforcement or just let requests through but mark them?

miles: idea: 
- mode: shadow (requests flow, no hard throttling)
- multiplier: 2-5x current per-key cap
- ttl: short window (1-4h)
- audit: full request/sample logging + flagged in console
- circuit: automatic fallback to hard cap if latency or error spike

ryan: Console concerns: must show who granted it, when, and give a one-click revoke. Also RBAC: only product+sales lead can request, ops must approve.

lina: Safety questions — if we let them bypass throttles what prevents noisy neighbor from killing runtime? We need to route shadowed keys to a separate pool or at least a canary lane.

miles: agree. plan: shadowed traffic -> shadow pool (smaller, isolated) with higher cost per-token and strict autoscale rules. If error rate > 3% or tail latency > 2s then auto-revoke.

sarah: From partner ops: they need sub-hour windows sometimes tied to campaign start times. Can TTL be cron-ish? e.g., start at 2024-05-15T09:00 for 3h.

miles: yeah support absolute windows or duration. We'll expose start/stop in the console and API.

devon: Metrics we need to emit: per-key tokens_allowed, tokens_used_shadow, shadow_multiplier, shadow_active:true/false, shadow_pool_id. Also a sample of proxied request ids for debugging.

ops-bot: [alert] acme-prod exceeded soft-cap (3/14 11:12) — throttled -> 429s — 12m spike, avg latency 420ms :eyes:

ryan: UX: add an audit trail entry that links to the logs and to the billing delta estimate for the window. Sales will want an upfront cost estimate.

miles: Proposed API surface (draft):

```
POST /v1/keys/:key/overrides
{
  "mode": "shadow",
  "multiplier": 3,
  "start_time": "2024-05-15T09:00:00Z",
  "ttl": "3h",
  "reason": "marketing burst - approved by ops",
  "notify_channels": ["#eng-oncall","#sales-acme"]
}
```

console-bot: created request id req_9f2b for override; requires ops approval.

lina: Implementation notes: we probably need a fast-path in router to check overrides cache (per-key), and ensure KV cache invalidation when revoke happens. Also ensure prefix caching is disabled for shadowed keys to avoid cost distortion.

devon: What about partners on dedicated pools? If a partner is on Dedicated, do we allow shadowing on top of their reserved capacity? Might double-count.

miles: For Dedicated, shadow requests should be billed separately and prefer burst pool; if they insist on using reserved capacity we require explicit finance signoff and manual accounting. Avoid auto-using reserved capacity.

ryan: Action items:
- miles: write RFC with config schema + RBAC matrix + console wireframes (ETA 2d)
- devon: prototype router check + metrics emission (ETA 3d)
- lina: failure/runbook for auto-revoke & canary pool (ETA 3d)
- ryan: console audit + revoke flow + billing estimate UI (ETA 4d)

miles: cool. I'll drop a short template for partner requests in #sales and tag ops. If anyone wants to pair on the RFC ping me. :thumbsup:

sarah: tagging @acme-ops so they're aware of the proposed flow.

console-bot: note: this thread recorded as ticket T-4891 (partner-shadow-overrides) for tracking.

miles: thanks everyone — we'll run this as a beta for 30 days and iterate.
